print.label: Print ISBN
print.summary: An identification number for the printed (physical) edition of a book.
uses: The book may be printed and sold through bookstores, fairs and libraries.
Registered in the National Library catalogue as a print edition.
Royalties are calculated from physical book sales.
print.suits: Best if you want a physical book to hold and sell directly.

electronic.label: Digital ISBN
electronic.summary: An identification number for the digital edition (ebook PDF/EPUB), also called an e-ISBN.
uses: The ebook may be sold on digital book platforms (e.g. Google Play Books) and on Tartila Book.
No printing cost, so it can be published faster.
Royalties are calculated from ebook sales.
electronic.suits: Best if you only want to publish an ebook.

both.label: Print + Digital ISBN
both.summary: Two ISBNs at once: one for the printed edition and one for the digital edition.
uses: The book is published in two formats: print and digital.
You receive both physical-book and ebook royalties.
Each format has its own ISBN, so it costs more than either one alone.
both.suits: Best if you want to reach print readers and digital readers alike.

chooseHint: The ISBN type sets the price, the publishing format and the kind of royalty in the MOU.
defaultPriceNote: The price shown is the Print ISBN price. The final price follows the ISBN type you choose.
